newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.100 cent per lb higher, livestock analysts said.

The June live cattle contract seasonally advanced after the April expiration Wednesday due to its usual discount to cash. But this year the recent weakness in cash cattle and declining boxed beef values will likely keep June from moving much higher, analysts said.
Back months will be influenced by grain markets and action in other livestock pits, sources said.

Feeder cattle futures were expected to be underpinned by recent strength in cash feeder cattle prices, which boosted the CME feeder cattle index to a 26-month high on Tuesday. Concern over cattle death losses in the Dakotas and northern Plains from storms and flooding were also expected to support futures in the feeder pit, analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was slipped $0.01 to $72.15 per cwt. The previous quote of $72.16 was the highest since February 22, 1995.
